title: Shared Counter, Many Hands
goal: Two handles, one score, two bumps. Share the counter and actually increment it.
hints: Moving score into judge leaves the later score.set with nothing — share, don't transfer.
judge.get() + 1 computes a number and lets it evaporate. Cells only change when someone calls set.
explanation: Rc shares the Cell (both handles reach ONE counter), and each set() lands where both can see it — 2. Moving score breaks the later lines (E0382). The evaporating bump is the quiet failure: computing get()+1 without set() changes nothing, compiles cleanly, and returns 1 — only the test complains. And spelling: score.clone() does the same cheap counter-bump as Rc::clone(&score), but reads like a deep copy — clone_on_ref_ptr keeps the syntax honest. Interior mutability plus shared ownership is powerful exactly because every piece is explicit.
